text:
Brock Faber is back from a skull fracture, and the night he scored in his first home game since, the Wild crowd let him hear it. NDTV Sports called the ovation loud, and The Athletic's Michael Russo wrote that his high standards haven't budged. He has two points in four games. Then Quinn Hughes went down, and Faber's job changed overnight: he played more than 29 minutes beside Jonas Brodin in the first game without Hughes.

Four games is too few to judge, and his early five-on-five numbers (43% of the expected goals, which measure the quality of chances) mostly say he is still finding his legs. Evolving-Hockey had him 23rd among 215 defensemen last season, 89th percentile for driving play. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking shows a high-volume shooter who doesn't always get inside. Russo has compared him to Charlie McAvoy, in look and in game. The next two weeks, with Hughes out, will show how much the Wild can lean on him.
